reason: Combining the dense knot with a nearby cold cloud may show whether the surviving clumps can form stars.
expectation: The cold gas may feed the knot and help it form new stars, though an intermediate gathering might come first.

alternatives.reason: The young stars interacting with dusty gas could address the other goal, but I want to follow the clumps first.

effect: The surviving clumps formed new stars, completing that goal; I’ll now follow the inherited dust.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the old pillars contribute to new stars beyond the nursery.
reason: The young stars may show what happens to dust that remains in their light.
expectation: Their radiation may heat or illuminate the dust, though I’m unsure what form the result will take.

alternatives.reason: The nursery outflow could instead show where some dust travels.

effect: The dust absorbs starlight and reradiates it in infrared; I’ll follow the dust carried outward next.
reaction: The distinction between glowing gas and warmed dust was interesting.
reason: Combining the nursery outflow with dusty gas should trace the other dust path mentioned in the introduction.
expectation: Some dust will be carried away from the nursery, perhaps into the outer stream.

alternatives.reason: The warmed dust could also enter the outflow, but I want to follow the separate outward path first.

effect: The outflow carries dust away, with some grains sheltered and others exposed; I’ll follow it into the outer gas.
reaction: The differing exposure of the grains makes me curious about their fate.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it follows the dust into the galaxy’s outer gas.
expectation: The dust will disperse into the hot outer gas; exposed grains may be altered or destroyed, but I’m unsure.

effect: The hot outer gas erodes many dust grains, completing the inherited-dust goal and the chapter.
reaction: The contrast between earlier warming and later destruction made the dust’s journey memorable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the surviving clumps into new stars was most worthwhile: it gave the old pillars a meaningful continuation beyond the nursery.

leastWorthwhile.text: Carrying dust outward felt the most straightforward; it mainly set up the more interesting encounter with hot gas.

surprise.text: Dust can absorb starlight and radiate in infrared without another star forming in the cloud.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary, though the final combination was the only offered action rather than a meaningful choice.

continue.text: Yes. I’d be interested in following how the dispersed gas and surviving dust participate in later encounters.
